conventions.convention: Finite differences use positive-minus-negative crossing resolutions and the product-of-signs alternating sum; D_0V=V. Type at most n means D_{n+1}V vanishes, and type at most -1 means the zero invariant.

Crossing signs are determinant signs of the ordered overpassing and underpassing projected tangents, with the projection-plane orientation fixed by the viewing normal; the positive Artin half twist has sign +1.

Framed singularity count includes both double points and simple normal-section zeroes. Framed normal-bundle clauses assume countable choice. A framing zero locally modeled by t e_1 is resolved toward ±e_2 in the oriented normal plane.

Both symbol modules use ordinary circle chord diagrams. The endpoint-slide relation is D_1-D_2+D_3-D_4=0. Isolated means intersecting no other chord; 1T is imposed only in the unframed quotient. Auxiliary framing dots are not module generators.
The converse integration assertion uses a separately identified external rational integration theorem; extension to a characteristic-zero field is a finite-dimensional scalar-extension argument.

load_bearing.statement: An invariant has type at most n if D_{n+1}V vanishes on every (n+1)-singular object in its category; framed singularities count both double points and framing zeroes.

The framed degree-n chord-diagram module is the free R-module on degree-n chord diagrams modulo all 4T relations. The unframed degree-n chord-diagram module is the free R-module on degree-n chord diagrams modulo 4T and 1T relations.

For a commutative ring R and n≥0, an invariant V of type at most n has representative-independent degree-n values on every degree-n chord diagram, independent also of zero-free framing class in the framed case under countable choice; these values annihilate every degree-n 4T generator.

For an unframed R-valued invariant V of type at most n≥1, D_nV(K)=0 whenever its chord diagram has a chord intersecting no other chord. Under countable choice, integer-valued framed self-linking has type at most 1 and derivative 2 on a one-chord diagram with blackboard framing.

For a commutative ring R and n≥0, the degree-n derivative of an unframed R-valued invariant of type at most n induces an R-linear functional modulo 4T and 1T; for a framed invariant under countable choice it induces an R-linear functional modulo 4T. Integer-valued framed self-linking has one-chord derivative 2.

concerns.concern: The framed double-point resolution says: “Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class.” It does not require transport through a small deformation of the original branchwise section, or otherwise specify the relative homotopy class of that extension. Extensions agreeing outside a resolution ball can differ by an arbitrary full normal twist on a branch interval. Twisting only the positive resolution changes its self-linking by one and therefore changes the proposed finite difference. As written, the extension instruction does not uniquely determine the framed derivative; this affects the framed type definition and downstream self-linking witness.

The diagram description calls D_1 a “one-crossing curl” and subsequently says “At the single crossing of D_1”. Its bottom closing Bézier, with control points (-1,0), (-1.15,-0.75), (1.15,-0.75), (1,0), intersects the returning Bézier with control points (0,-0.42), (0,-0.76), (0.50,-0.70), (1,0) twice away from their common endpoint. Numerical segment-intersection checks locate these extra intersections near (0.044607,-0.562069) and (0.509942,-0.501289). Neither has over/under data. Thus the displayed witness is not the claimed regular one-crossing diagram, although the separate textual R1 counterexample is sound.
